transcript:
Meeting header:
2026-03-01 10:00 UTC | Duration: 57m | Attendees: Alex Carter, Priya Shah, Liam Brooks (Redwood) — Maya Chen, Diego Ramos, Priyanka Gupta, Samir Patel (DataWave)

Auto-generated summary: review of this week's benchmark runs; discussed apparent 15-25% throughput delta against baseline provider, identified test config mismatch (batch size and token distribution), agreed on cache-enabled runs and quantized model checks.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Alex): hey everybody, thanks for joining, can you hear me okay?
00:03 Speaker 2 (Maya): yep, loud and clear
00:05 Speaker 1 (Alex): great, so quick agenda — run through the numbers we pushed yesterday, call out the diffs versus the baseline provider, go over config changes priya proposed, and lock next steps. we have about fifty seven minutes so let's keep it focused.
00:18 Speaker 3 (Priya): quick note — i'll share the slide with the P50/P95/P99 charts in chat, and the raw logs are in the spreadsheet alex linked.
00:25 Speaker 4 (Diego): thanks, i pulled the sheet. first question, are we comparing identical model checkpoints? baseline had "BaseModel-v2" listed. are we using the same quantization and context window?
00:36 Speaker 2 (Maya): yes this is important because our users run 512 token average — the baseline runs we saw used 256 which will skew latency and throughput.
00:44 Speaker 1 (Alex): good catch — so the baseline provider's run note says 256 token average, batching 8, no KV cache. our run was 512 avg, batching 4, KV cache off. that explains a lot of the delta.
00:56 Speaker 3 (Priya): right, when we re-ran with a 256 token mix and batching 8 we got throughput within 8% of baseline on same GPU class, with P95 latency about 10% lower. but with your production 512 mix, we still see Redwood outperforming on P50 but throughput drops.
01:10 Speaker 4 (Diego): so basically we were comparing apples to oranges. can you walk through the numbers — P50 P95 P99 for the 512 test and the baseline 256 for both providers?
01:18 Speaker 1 (Alex): sure — i'll read the headline numbers then priya will share details. Redwood (512 mix, batching=4): P50 45ms, P95 220ms, P99 480ms, throughput 220 requests/min on the instance we used. Baseline provider (256 mix, batching=8, no cache): reported P50 40ms, P95 300ms, P99 700ms, throughput 260 requests/min. note baseline P95/P99 looked worse even with smaller tokens.
01:47 Speaker 3 (Priya): the key is the KV cache — when we enable prefix caching on Redwood and tune batching to continuous batching at workload, the 512 mix P95 comes down to ~170ms and throughput rises to 310 req/min. we validated on the same GPU family.
02:03 Speaker 5 (Priyanka): sorry, can you remind me — what do you mean by KV cache? our infra team is worried about memory blowouts if everyone caches large prefixes.
02:12 Speaker 3 (Priya): yes, good point. KV cache stores past key/value attention state so subsequent tokens for the same session don't recompute earlier layers. it's per-session and we give controls on eviction and size. there's a tradeoff — more cache can increase memory but reduces per-token compute and latency. we can set ttl and max entries to bound memory.
02:31 Speaker 4 (Diego): is that safe for multi-tenant? we need encryption and logs.
02:36 Speaker 1 (Alex): in Dedicated and Private modes we support KMS-wrapped keys, per-customer eviction policies, and audit logs. for the POC we can enable cache for only the test sessions to show the performance delta.
02:47 Speaker 6 (Samir): side question, did you test quantized weights? we saw some quality drift when other vendors used 4-bit.
02:54 Speaker 3 (Priya): yes, we ran int8 and int4 variants — int8 gave ~12% latency improvement w/o measurable quality drop on our eval set; int4 saved more but in some prompts it introduced edge-case hallucinations. we recommend int8 for production-like POCs; we can run targeted quality evals if you want.
03:12 Speaker 2 (Maya): quality is a blocker for us. happy to test int8 but want examples where int4 fails. can you add that to the action items?
03:19 Speaker 1 (Alex): noted.

03:30 Speaker 3 (Priya): i'm dropping the dashboard link now — and the annotated diff. quick pause to call out test config drift: baseline provider used a different tokenization path, and their batch counting was per micro-batch vs our reported aggregated batch — small differences that inflate throughput numbers.
03:51 Speaker 4 (Diego): we were also using a different concurrency pattern in the harness — our harness did a bursty send which made baseline look better in short windows.
03:58 Speaker 3 (Priya): yep exactly. for fairness we recommend: use 512 token distribution CSV that you provided, consistent concurrency (steady-state at target QPS), run for 30 minutes for steady-state and collect P50/P95/P99, and include cache/no-cache variants.
04:16 Speaker 2 (Maya): agree. so what are the next runs you propose?
04:20 Speaker 3 (Priya): plan A: replicate baseline config (256, batching=8, no-cache) on Redwood to show parity. Plan B: run production config (512 avg, steady concurrency) with cache enabled and int8 quantization. Plan C: run long-run 90m stability test to check tail latencies and memory growth.
04:36 Speaker 1 (Alex): we can start Plan A today and Priya will run Plan B and C this week if Diego can provide the final token distribution and concurrency script.
04:46 Speaker 4 (Diego): i can drop the CSV and script by tomorrow EOD.
04:49 Speaker 6 (Samir): for billing, can you estimate cost delta if we go cache heavy? our CFO will want to see delta between baseline and Redwood.
04:57 Speaker 1 (Alex): sure — caching reduces compute but adds memory footprint; in Dedicated pricing the unit cost shifts — i'll include a cost model in the spreadsheet: compute cost, memory premium, and expected cost per 1M tokens.
05:10 Speaker 5 (Priyanka): on the private deployment side, we need SOC2 evidence and SAML for SSO; legal will want audit logs. what's your timeline for that?
05:20 Speaker 1 (Alex): we have SOC2 type 2 in our compliance pack, support SAML/SSO via SAML 2.0, and we log all admin and API events with optional retention. i will share the security pack after this call.
05:31 Speaker 2 (Maya): great — we'll route that through our security folks.
05:34 Speaker 3 (Priya): back to numbers — i also want to call out GPU selection. we ran on the A100-equivalent instance; the baseline summary may have used a V100-class or different memory. matching GPU matters for throughput per card.
05:48 Speaker 4 (Diego): the baseline invoice says "gpu: T4" which is older, so not a fair comparison.
05:53 Speaker 3 (Priya): right — once we align GPU, token mix, batch size, and cache, the delta shrinks and in many configs Redwood gives lower P95.
06:05 Speaker 6 (Samir): any regression or hard failure during your runs? memory leaks, OOMs?
06:10 Speaker 3 (Priya): only in one long int4 run we saw some OOMs when KV cache plus large session retention was enabled; that's why we propose eviction policies for stability. Plan C will measure memory growth.
06:23 Speaker 1 (Alex): quick pause, i'm going to read the prioritized next steps so we have alignment: Alex sends annotated benchmark sheet + cost model; Priya runs cache+int8 and long stability runs and shares raw logs; Diego provides token distribution + concurrency harness; Maya to introduce security contact for POI. any edits?
06:39 Speaker 2 (Maya): correct. also can we make sure the spreadsheets include the exact CLI commands used for each run? the baseline doc didn't, which made replication hard.
06:48 Speaker 3 (Priya): yes we'll add the harness commands and docker image tags.
06:52 Speaker 4 (Diego): regarding quality metrics — can you also include eval set pass rates and a short example prompt set where int4 broke?
06:59 Speaker 3 (Priya): yes will do.

07:10 Speaker 1 (Alex): short administrative: what's your decision timeline for Dedicated/Private?
07:15 Speaker 2 (Maya): we want POC results and security signoff in two sprints, so aiming to decide by mid April.
07:22 Speaker 6 (Samir): finance also wants an estimate for committed capacity pricing if we choose Dedicated — can you provide a ballpark?
07:29 Speaker 1 (Alex): yes i'll include a tiered pricing table in the follow-up.
07:32 Speaker 3 (Priya): one more thing — we noticed a minor tokenization mismatch where emojis in your prompts expanded token counts; that impacted a few runs. Diego, maybe sanitize or normalize before running.
07:44 Speaker 4 (Diego): good catch, we'll normalize.

07:55 Speaker 1 (Alex): any final questions?
07:57 Speaker 2 (Maya): no, thanks.
07:58 Speaker 1 (Alex): ok we'll send the sheet and schedule the Plan A replicate run today. thanks everyone.
08:02 Speaker 3 (Priya): thanks all.

(Transcript ends — occasional transcription errors present; speaker labels may not perfectly align with meeting participants.)
